 J U D G M E N T

The appellants herein are the petitioners in O.P.(Div)

No.976/2013 on the file of the Family Court, Mavelikara. The

appeal is filed against the judgment dated 19.10.2013 in the

original petition. The original petition was filed by the

appellants for a decree of dissolution of marriage by mutual

consent under Section 10A of the Divorce Act, 1869. The

original petition was filed before the Family Court, Alappuzha.

After the establishment of the Family Court at Mavelikara, the

same was transferred to the said court. The court below by the

impugned order held that the period of separate living of the

spouse should be two years in the case of an application under

 Section 10A of the Divorce Act, 1869 and hence the application

filed by the petitioners/appellants under Section 10A of the

Divorce Act, 1869 is not allowable.

2. Due to clerical mistake, which did not come to the

notice of the petitioners or to the notice of their counsel, it is

MAT Appeal No.62 of 2014
 2

averred in the petition that the parties are living separately

from 20.08.2012. The petition for dissolution of marriage by

mutual consent under Section 10A of the Divorce Act was filed

on 14.03.2013. They filed a proof affidavit before the court. In

that affidavit also it is stated that they are living separately

from 20.08.2012 onwards. The learned Judge held that the

period of separation must be two years or more. The present

petition for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent is before

the period stipulated under Section 10A of the Divorce Act.

3. The learned counsel for the appellants/petitioners

placed reliance on the decision reported in Saumya Ann

Thomas v. Union of India [2010(1) KLT 869] which had

declared the "two years" waiting period under Section 10A of

the Divorce Act is unconstitutional and that it shall be read

down to a period of "one year". The learned counsel submitted

that the date of separation averred in the petition as

20.08.2012 is a clerical error and that the correct date of

separation is 20.01.2012. If 20.01.2012 is the date of

separation, the application for dissolution of marriage by

mutual consent is within time. The learned counsel for the

petitioners/appellants seeks to amend the pleadings for

correcting the mistake in date.

4. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of

the view that an opportunity shall be given to the petitioners to

amend the pleadings and substantiate their contentions.

In the result, the appeal is allowed and the impugned

judgment is set aside. The case is remanded for fresh

consideration in accordance with law. The petitioners/

appellants are at liberty to amend the pleadings by filing

necessary application before the court below, if so advised.

The petitioners/appellants shall appear before the court below

on 18.02.2014. The court below shall consider and dispose of

the original petition within a period of two months.

ALEXANDER THOMAS, JUDGE




AV
